causal:influence:abat_activity:negative:.evidence: GABA-transaminase deficiency (ABAT LoF, OMIM 613163): Jaeken et al. (1984) Neuropediatrics 15:165-168 (elevated CSF GABA in ABAT deficiency); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (GABA transamination uses alpha-ketoglutarate as amino-acceptor; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (GABA catabolism: GABA-T reaction stoichiometry). Intervention: do(ABAT LoF). | intervention: genetic loss-of-function of ABAT (GABA-transaminase deficiency, OMIM 613163)
causal:influence:abat_activity:negative:.mechanism: 4-Aminobutyrate aminotransferase (ABAT/GABA-transaminase) catalyzes GABA + alpha-ketoglutarate -> succinic semialdehyde + glutamate, consuming alpha-KG as the amino-acceptor. Active ABAT consumes CSF alpha-KG; ABAT deficiency (GABA-transaminase deficiency, OMIM 613163) spares alpha-KG from this transamination, raising the CSF alpha-KG pool.

(2015) Nucleosides Nucleotides Nucleic Acids 34:622–634 (ATIC deficiency, OMIM 608688: AICA-riboside / AICAR accumulates in body fluids); OMIM 608688 (AICA-ribosiduria, ATIC LoF); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (de-novo purine synthesis: AICAR -[ATIC]-> FAICAR -> IMP). | intervention: genetic LoF of ATIC (AICA-ribosiduria / AICAR transformylase deficiency, OMIM 608688)

causal:influence:aldosterone:positive:ce.evidence: "Aldosterone Increases Potassium Uptake into Cells. Increased potassium intake also stimulates secretion of aldosterone, which increases cell potassium uptake" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 29 (Renal Regulation) Table 29-1, p 366

causal:influence:alveolar_surface_tensio.evidence: "lungs inflated with saline have a much larger compliance (are easier to distend) than do air-filled lungs ... the saline abolished the surface tension forces but presumably did not affect the tissue forces"; "a low surface tension in the alveoli increases the compliance of the lung" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 7)
causal:influence:alveolar_surface_tensio.mechanism: surface tension of the alveolar lining film adds a recoil/collapsing force; lowering it (e.g. saline-filling abolishes surface tension) makes the lung easier to distend, raising compliance

causal:influence:aprt_activity:positive:.evidence: Edvardsson et al., Am J Kidney Dis 2013 (APRT deficiency OMIM 614723: 2,8-DHA crystal nephropathy, CKD progression, ESRD in ~15% at diagnosis); PMID 24940675 (2,8-DHA urolithiasis review confirming progressive GFR decline if untreated); PMC4560835 (2,8-DHA nephropathy: recurrent post-transplant allograft failure; crystal deposition confirmed). | intervention: do(APRT LoF, OMIM 614723): adenine not salvaged; 2,8-DHA crystals deposit in renal tubules; progressive nephropathy; GFR falls. | intervention: do(APRT LoF, 2,8-DHA urolithiasis/nephropathy, OMIM 614723) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:aprt_activity:positive:.mechanism: APRT (adenine phosphoribosyltransferase) salvages adenine (with PRPP) back to AMP; APRT deficiency (OMIM 614723) prevents adenine salvage, leaving free adenine to be oxidised by xanthine oxidase to 8-hydroxyadenine and then 2,8-dihydroxyadenine (2,8-DHA). 2,8-DHA is virtually insoluble in urine at any physiological pH, crystallising in the renal tubules and collecting system to form stones and cause 2,8-DHA crystal nephropathy. Progressive tubular and glomerular damage from crystal deposition leads to chronic kidney disease and declining GFR (approximately 15% present with ESRD at diagnosis). Higher APRT activity salvages adenine away from the 2,8-DHA-forming pathway, preventing crystal nephropathy and preserving GFR.

causal:influence:arginase_activity:negat.evidence: Lehninger, urea cycle step 5 (arginase); Harrison's / OMMBID argininemia (ARG1 deficiency) — HYPERargininemia
causal:influence:arginase_activity:negat.mechanism: arginase (ARG1) hydrolyzes arginine -> ornithine + urea; reduced arginase activity (argininemia) causes arginine to accumulate

causal:influence:argininosuccinate_synth.evidence: Citrullinemia type I (ASS1 deficiency, OMIM 215700) — markedly elevated plasma and CSF citrulline is the biochemical hallmark; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (citrullinemia: ASS1 deficiency causes severe citrulline accumulation in plasma, urine, and CSF); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (urea cycle step 3: ASS1 condenses citrulline + aspartate -> argininosuccinate). | intervention: do(ASS1 LoF) — citrullinemia type I
causal:influence:argininosuccinate_synth.mechanism: Argininosuccinate synthetase (ASS1) consumes citrulline + aspartate -> argininosuccinate in the urea cycle; ASS1 deficiency (citrullinemia type I) blocks this step, causing citrulline to accumulate markedly in plasma and CSF.

causal:influence:argininosuccinate_synth.evidence: Lehninger, urea cycle step 3 (ASS1 forms argininosuccinate)
causal:influence:argininosuccinate_synth.mechanism: ASS1 produces argininosuccinate; reduced activity lowers its formation

causal:influence:asns_activity:positive:.evidence: Asparagine synthetase deficiency (ASNS, OMIM 615574) — low CSF and plasma asparagine is the biochemical hallmark; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (ASNS deficiency: severely depleted CSF asparagine); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (asparagine synthetase: aspartate + glutamine + ATP -> asparagine). | intervention: do(ASNS LoF) — asparagine synthetase deficiency: CSF asparagine falls
causal:influence:asns_activity:positive:.mechanism: Asparagine synthetase (ASNS) catalyzes the ATP-dependent amidation of aspartate to asparagine using glutamine as the nitrogen donor; de novo asparagine synthesis is the primary source of asparagine in the CNS; ASNS deficiency severely depletes plasma and CSF asparagine.

causal:influence:aspartylglucosaminidase.evidence: Aspartylglucosaminuria (AGU), OMIM:208400 — AGA LoF causes neurodegeneration with CSF aspartylglucosamine elevation, reflecting CNS lysosomal storage
causal:influence:aspartylglucosaminidase.mechanism: RHEA:11544 (EC 3.5.1.26): N(4)-(beta-N-acetyl-D-glucosaminyl)-L-asparagine + H2O = N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminylamine + L-aspartate; substrate accumulates in lysosomes of CNS cells and is detectable in CSF

causal:influence:bace1_activity:positive.evidence: Kennedy et al. (2016) Science 352:aad3279 (verubecestat BACE1 inhibitor: dose-dependent reduction of CSF Abeta40/42 in humans); Vassar et al. (1999) Science 286:735–741 (BACE1 is the beta-secretase for APP cleavage); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (Alzheimer disease: Abeta production by BACE1 and gamma-secretase). | intervention: pharmacological BACE1 inhibition (verubecestat/atabecestat/lanabecestat clinical trials): do(BACE1 inhibitor) -> CSF Abeta falls
causal:influence:bace1_activity:positive.mechanism: BACE1 (beta-secretase 1) cleaves amyloid precursor protein (APP) at the beta-site to produce the C99 fragment, which gamma-secretase then cuts to release amyloid-beta peptides (Abeta); more BACE1 activity generates more Abeta. BACE1 inhibitors (verubecestat, atabecestat, lanabecestat) reduce CSF Abeta by ~50–80% in human clinical trials.

causal:influence:bisphosphoglycerate_mut.evidence: BPGM deficiency (OMIM:222800): patients have essentially zero 2,3-BPG in red cells and erythrocytosis — direct genetic proof that BPGM activity controls erythrocyte 2,3-BPG. Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-5.03.4 (Summary): 'bisphosphoglycerate, all allosteric ligands... shift the binding curves of Hb for oxygen to the right' — 2,3-BPG is the direct product of BPGM. | intervention: do(bisphosphoglycerate_mutase_activity LoF): BPGM deficiency (OMIM:222800) abolishes erythrocyte 2,3-BPG; altitude / hypoxia increases BPGM expression and raises 2,3-BPG
causal:influence:bisphosphoglycerate_mut.mechanism: Bisphosphoglycerate mutase (BPGM) converts 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (a glycolytic intermediate) to 2,3-BPG within erythrocytes; BPGM is the sole synthetic enzyme for 2,3-BPG. Loss-of-function mutations in BPGM (bisphosphoglycerate mutase deficiency, OMIM:222800) abolish 2,3-BPG synthesis, causing a near-complete absence of erythrocyte 2,3-BPG. Gain of enzyme activity (e.g. high altitude acclimatization) raises 2,3-BPG, shifting the oxygen-dissociation curve rightward.

causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.evidence: XLA (OMIM 300755): all immunoglobulin isotypes absent; Janeway's Immunobiology 10th ed., 'Defects in B cell development'. | intervention: do(BTK LoF) — no mature B cells; no circulating IgD
causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.mechanism: BTK deficiency blocks maturation of B cells; IgD is co-expressed with IgM on mature naive B cells, and without any mature B cells in XLA, circulating IgD is absent.

causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.evidence: XLA (OMIM 300755): absent IgE; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Primary immunodeficiency diseases'. | intervention: do(BTK LoF) — B cell maturation arrest; no IgE-secreting plasma cells
causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.mechanism: BTK deficiency abolishes all B cell development; IgE — like all other isotypes — is absent in XLA because no plasma cells of any isotype form.

causal:influence:camp_level:positive:pka.evidence: BioModels BIOMD0000000165 Saucerman et al. 2006 PNAS 103:12923 (PubMed 16905651): cAMP-dependent PKA activation; also MODEL1006230118 Saucerman et al. 2003 (PubMed 12972422); Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology. | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-37.2 (37.2: How Hormones Work): 'cAMP, in turn, activates a group of proteins called protein kinases, which transfer a phosphate group from ATP to a substrate molecule in a process called phosphorylation.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-9.2 (9.2: Propagation of the Signal): 'The main role of cAMP in cells is to bind to and activate an enzyme called cAMP-dependent kinase (A-kinase)'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-9.3 (9.3: Response to the Signal): 'Cyclic AMP activates PKA (protein kinase A)' [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:camp_level:positive:pka.mechanism: cAMP (quality: concentration) binds PKA regulatory subunits (disposition: allosteric release -> process: dissociation of catalytic subunits) -> quality: free PKA-C catalytic activity

causal:influence:capillary_hydrostatic_p.evidence: "The increased cardiac output increases the capillary pressure so that fluid begins to transude out of the capillaries into the tissues" Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch w07, p 242
causal:influence:capillary_hydrostatic_p.mechanism: Higher capillary hydrostatic pressure increases the net filtration pressure driving fluid from capillary lumen into interstitial space (Starling forces)

causal:influence:cathepsin_d_activity:ne.evidence: CLN10 disease / congenital NCL (OMIM:610127); Siintola et al. 2006 Ann Neurol (CTSD mutations cause congenital NCL); PMC7158922 (ERT with recombinant pro-CTSD corrects defective proteolysis and reduces NCL storage material, confirming causal direction); PMC9270453 (CTSD deficiency causes saposin and proteinopathy-related protein accumulation in CNS); MedlinePlus CTSD: 'CTSD gene mutations lead to complete absence of cathepsin D, causing protein/fat accumulation in lysosomes'. | intervention: CTSD loss-of-function (CLN10/congenital NCL): do(cathepsin_d_activity = down) -> lysosomal saposin C/D and ceroid lipofuscin accumulate (up).
causal:influence:cathepsin_d_activity:ne.mechanism: Cathepsin D (CTSD) is the principal lysosomal aspartic protease responsible for degrading saposin C, saposin D, and other lysosomal substrates during autophagy and endocytosis. Loss of CTSD activity (CLN10 disease) causes lysosomal accumulation of saposins C and D, ATP synthase subunit c, and other undegraded proteins forming ceroid lipofuscin storage material — the pathological hallmark of congenital NCL.

causal:influence:cd40l_signaling_activit.evidence: Hyper-IgM syndrome type 1 (HIGM1; OMIM 308230): CD40LG loss-of-function causes absent serum IgG, IgA, IgE with normal/elevated IgM; Janeway's Immunobiology 10th ed., 'T cell-dependent B cell responses'; PMID 24308834 (Expert Rev Clin Immunol 2014). | intervention: do(CD40LG LoF) — defective T–B cell costimulation; no class-switch to IgG; IgG absent in HIGM1 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cd40l_signaling_activit.mechanism: CD40L on activated T helper cells signals CD40 on B cells to trigger class-switch recombination from IgM to IgG; CD40L deficiency (HIGM1) abolishes IgG production while IgM accumulates.

causal:influence:cd4_t_cell_count:positi.evidence: Fauci AS et al 1996 Ann Intern Med 124:654 — CD4 count is the primary surrogate marker for T cell immune activity in HIV disease; Glare EM & Quinn KM 2016: CD4+ count < 200 cells/μL defines AIDS by immunological collapse of T cell-mediated immunity; Mosmann TR & Coffman RL 1989 Ann Rev Immunol 7:145 — CD4+ Th cells are obligate activators of both cytotoxic T cell and humoral arms; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §21.3 (Adaptive Immune Response): 'helper T cells serve as the master regulators of the adaptive immune response'. | intervention: do(cd4_t_cell_count -) — HIV infection depletes CD4+ T cells, proportionally collapsing T cell immune activity; do(cd4_t_cell_count +) — antiretroviral therapy restores CD4+ count and T cell immune activity.
causal:influence:cd4_t_cell_count:positi.mechanism: CD4+ helper T cells are the master coordinators of adaptive immune responses: they provide cytokine help (IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-4) to cytotoxic T cells, B cells, and macrophages, and are required for effective T cell-mediated immune activity. When CD4+ T cell count falls (as in HIV/AIDS), T cell-mediated immune activity collapses, leading to opportunistic infections. The causal direction is: CD4+ T cell number sets the ceiling on T cell immune activity.

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:osteo.evidence: "glucocorticoids also have a strong negative effect on bone formation by suppressing expression of IGF1 in bone cells and by shifting marrow stromal cells into the fat lineage rather than down the osteoblast differentiation pathway." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 30 (glucocorticoid-induced bone loss)
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:osteo.mechanism: glucocorticoid acts on osteoblast GR (quality: plasma cortisol → disposition: GR signalling → process: suppressed IGF1/osteoblast differentiation, stromal-to-adipocyte shift, osteoblast apoptosis → quality: reduced osteoblast bone-formation activity); basis of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:pitui.evidence: HumMod adrenal feedback; Boron & Boulpaep — glucocorticoid suppression of ACTH | pharmacological do(): the dexamethasone suppression test — dexamethasone (GR agonist / cortisol analog) directly suppresses pituitary ACTH secretion and lowers cortisol (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dexamethasone_suppression_test, opened) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-090 (17.3: Hormones): 'glucocorticoid concentrations in the blood rise, the hypothalamus and pituitary gland reduce their signaling to the adrenal glands' — glucocorticoid negative feedback on ACTH
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:pitui.mechanism: cortisol (glucocorticoid) binds pituitary corticotrope glucocorticoid receptors and suppresses ACTH secretion (fast + delayed negative feedback)

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:thymi.evidence: PMID 39315105; (Abstract); “These regimens produced a marked acute thymic involution in mice, which correlated with elevated serum glucocorticoid levels and a diminishment of naive T cells in the periphery.” | Elevated glucocorticoids (cortisol) cause acute thymic involution, supporting do(cortisol up) -> thymus mass down (-). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:thymi.mechanism: cortisol -> glucocorticoid receptor in thymocytes -> increased thymocyte (CD4+CD8+) apoptosis -> acute thymic involution / reduced thymus mass

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.evidence: "Angiotensinogen synthesis is increased by glucocorticoids" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 15, p. 496
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.mechanism: glucocorticoids increase hepatic angiotensinogen synthesis → elevated plasma angiotensinogen

causal:influence:csf_glucose:positive:ce.evidence: PMC12002639 (Seizure and redox rescue in a model of glucose transport deficiency: GLUT1-DS seizures result from after-discharge neuronal firing caused by post-stimulus ATP reductions and impaired Na+/K+-ATPase); OMIM 606777 (GLUT1 deficiency syndrome, De Vivo disease; SLC2A1 LoF; hypoglycorrhachia); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (CSF glucose: normal 60-70% of plasma, reduced by GLUT1 deficiency). | intervention: SLC2A1 biallelic loss-of-function (GLUT1 deficiency syndrome, OMIM 606777): do(SLC2A1 activity DOWN) -> CSF glucose DOWN -> neuronal ATP DOWN -> seizures | intervention: SLC2A1 biallelic loss-of-function (GLUT1 deficiency syndrome, De Vivo disease, OMIM 606777) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:csf_glucose:positive:ce.mechanism: CSF glucose is the primary metabolic substrate for neurons (transported via GLUT3 at the neuronal membrane). Low CSF glucose (hypoglycorrhachia) — as in GLUT1 deficiency syndrome — starves neurons of their principal energy source; experimental and clinical evidence shows that GLUT1-DS seizures result from post-stimulus ATP reductions and impaired Na+/K+-ATPase function. Higher CSF glucose increases neuronal glycolytic flux and oxidative phosphorylation, raising cellular ATP concentration.

causal:influence:csf_tetrahydrobiopterin.evidence: Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (CSF 5-HIAA reflects central serotonin turnover; low in BH4 defects); Lehninger (tryptophan hydroxylase requires BH4)
causal:influence:csf_tetrahydrobiopterin.mechanism: BH4 is also cofactor for tryptophan hydroxylase (serotonin synthesis); 5-HIAA is the terminal serotonin catabolite, so reduced BH4 lowers CSF 5-HIAA (serotonergic turnover marker)

causal:influence:cystinosin_transport_ac.evidence: Gahl WA et al. NEJM 2002 346:1456-1463 — nephropathic cystinosis: natural history of GFR decline; renal Fanconi syndrome is the earliest manifestation, progressing to ESRD. GeneReviews NBK1400 (cystinosis): 'Kidneys are initially affected with generalised proximal tubular dysfunction (renal Fanconi syndrome), then disease rapidly affects glomeruli and progresses towards end-stage renal failure'. PMC4374958 (Amer J Physiol Renal 2015) — endo-lysosomal dysfunction in cystinosis-deficient proximal tubular cells. OMIM 219800 (nephropathic cystinosis). | intervention: do(CTNS biallelic LoF) = nephropathic cystinosis, OMIM 219800: lysosomal cystine accumulates → Fanconi syndrome → progressive GFR loss | intervention: do(CTNS biallelic LoF) — nephropathic cystinosis, OMIM 219800
causal:influence:cystinosin_transport_ac.mechanism: Cystinosin (CTNS) is the H+-driven lysosomal cystine transporter that exports free cystine from lysosomes to the cytosol. CTNS LoF (nephropathic cystinosis) abolishes lysosomal cystine export, causing progressive intralysosomal cystine crystal accumulation in all cells, most critically in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells. Crystal accumulation causes oxidative stress, impaired autophagy, and tubular cell apoptosis, producing Fanconi syndrome (generalised proximal tubular dysfunction). Progressive tubular and glomerular injury then causes sustained GFR decline, with untreated patients reaching end-stage renal disease in the first two decades. Sign: more cystinosin activity → better lysosomal cystine clearance → preserved tubular function → higher GFR (do(CTNS LoF) = GFR falls).

causal:influence:d2hgdh_activity:negativ.evidence: Struys et al. (2005) J Inherit Metab Dis 28:963–972 (D-2-HGA type I: D2HGDH LoF, elevated D-2-HG in CSF); OMIM 600721 (D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria type I, D2HGDH deficiency); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (2-hydroxyglutarate as metabolite in TCA-cycle vicinity). | intervention: genetic LoF of D2HGDH (D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria type I, OMIM 600721)
causal:influence:d2hgdh_activity:negativ.mechanism: D-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase (D2HGDH) catalyses oxidation of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2-HG) to 2-oxoglutarate (alpha-ketoglutarate); higher D2HGDH activity consumes D-2-HG. LoF (D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria type I) causes D-2-HG accumulation in urine, plasma and CSF.

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (pyrimidine catabolism: 5,6-dihydrothymine -[DPYS]-> N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate); OMIM 222748 (dihydropyrimidinase deficiency, DPYS LoF: dihydrouracil and dihydrothymine accumulate in CSF/urine). | intervention: genetic LoF of DPYS (dihydropyrimidinase deficiency, OMIM 222748)
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.mechanism: Dihydropyrimidinase (DPYS) ring-opens 5,6-dihydrothymine to N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate; more DPYS activity consumes dihydrothymine. LoF (dihydropyrimidinase deficiency) causes dihydrouracil and dihydrothymine accumulation in CSF.
N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate (ureidoisobutyrate) is the DPYS product of dihydrothymine.

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.mechanism: DPYD reduces thymine to 5,6-dihydrothymine; more DPYD consumes more thymine.

causal:influence:distal_tubular_flow_rat.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.29 (Renal Regulation of Potassium, Calcium, Phosphate, and Magnesium; Integration of Renal Mechanisms for Control of Blood Volume and Extracellular Fluid Volume) §Increased Distal Tubular Flow Rate Stimulates Potassium Secretion: “A rise in distal tubular flow rate, as occurs with volume expansion, high sodium intake, or diuretic drug treatment, stimulates potassium secretion”
causal:influence:distal_tubular_flow_rat.mechanism: high luminal flow flushes secreted K+ downstream, lowering luminal K+ and preserving the diffusion gradient that drives principal-cell K+ secretion into the tubule

causal:influence:dystrophin_level:negati.evidence: PMID 6780020; (Abstract); “The ratio of 3-methylhistidine:creatinine excretion, a measure of the fractional catabolic rate of myofibrillar protein was increased in severe injury, thyrotoxicosis, neoplastic disease, prednisolone administration, and sometimes Duchenne muscular dystrophy.” | Urinary 3-methylhistidine excretion rises with increased myofibrillar protein catabolism and is increased in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (dystrophin loss), supporting do(dystrophin down) -> 3-MeHis up (sign -). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:dystrophin_level:negati.mechanism: Dystrophin loss (DMD, a natural single-gene do()) -> sarcolemmal fragility/myofibrillar damage -> accelerated actin/myosin (myofibrillar) catabolism -> increased release of the non-reutilized post-translational residue 3-methylhistidine -> increased urinary 3-methylhistidine excretion (lower dystrophin -> higher 3-MeHis).

causal:influence:endothelial_akt_signali.evidence: AOP-Wiki KER uuid 47ca4026-7f6f-4c3c-ad98-b72b5aed093d; AOP: 'Peptide Oxidation Leading to Hypertension'. No PMID supplied. Mechanism: AKT phosphorylates NOS3 Ser1177 -> NO production (Dimmeler et al., Nature 1999 PMID 10421379; Fulton et al., Nature 1999 PMID 10421380). Sign '+': AKT activity up -> eNOS activated -> NO production up. *** DRAFT FOR REVIEW (imported) ***
causal:influence:endothelial_akt_signali.mechanism: AKT1 (RAC-alpha kinase) is activated by upstream PI3K signalling (e.g. shear stress, insulin, VEGF) and phosphorylates eNOS (NOS3) at Ser1177, displacing the inhibitory calmodulin and activating NO synthesis. Decreased AKT/eNOS signalling reduces eNOS phosphorylation at Ser1177, impairing NO production.

causal:influence:endothelial_et1_secreti.evidence: OmniPath intercell EDN1->EDNRA is_stimulation=True (consensus; refs incl. Yanagisawa 1988 Nature 332:411, PMID 2451132); Boron & Boulpaep | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-106 (19.2: Heart Anatomy): 'Endothelins are potent vasoconstrictors and, in a normal individual, establish a homeostatic balance with other vasoconstrictors and vasodilators.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-111 (20.2: Structure and Function of Blood Vessels): endothelins constrict smooth muscle in vessel walls [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:endothelial_et1_secreti.mechanism: ET-1 binds EDNRA on smooth muscle (Gq/PLC-beta -> IP3 -> SR Ca2+ release) -> Ca2+/calmodulin -> MLCK -> MLC phosphorylation; sustained contraction

causal:influence:esophageal_luminal_pres.evidence: Mittal & Bhalla, J Clin Gastroenterol 2004; PMC2728598 — 'Secondary peristalsis is entirely due to peripheral mechanisms' triggered by esophageal distension; StatPearls: Physiology, Lower Esophageal Sphincter (NBK557452) — 'esophageal peristalsis promotes esophageal acid clearance by removing refluxate'; esophageal luminal pressure is the proximate mechanosensory stimulus for secondary peristalsis. | intervention: do(esophageal_luminal_pressure↑) — as occurs during swallowing or esophageal distension (e.g. achalasia manometry, esophageal balloon distension experiments)
causal:influence:esophageal_luminal_pres.mechanism: Increased esophageal luminal pressure (distension by a swallowed bolus) activates mechanosensory afferents in the esophageal wall, which trigger secondary peristalsis through enteric and vagal neural circuits. Secondary peristalsis is entirely peripherally (ENS) driven by esophageal distension and represents a key component of GI motility (the rate of peristaltic propagation along the gut).

causal:influence:fads1_activity:positive.evidence: Stoffel et al., PNAS 2008 (Fads1 knockout mice: reduced arachidonic acid); Lattka et al., Br J Nutr 2010 (FADS1 GWAS variants control arachidonic acid levels in plasma); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Ch. 21 (PUFA desaturation pathway). | intervention: FADS1 loss-of-function (reduced delta-5 desaturase activity in FADS1 variant carriers): FADS1 LoF -> reduced conversion of DGLA to arachidonic acid -> reduced plasma arachidonic acid [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:fads1_activity:positive.mechanism: FADS1 (acyl-CoA delta-5 desaturase) converts dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA, C20:3n-6) to arachidonic acid (C20:4n-6) by inserting a double bond at the delta-5 position. FADS1 deficiency or reduced activity (genetic FADS1 variants) results in reduced plasma arachidonic acid and accumulation of DGLA.

causal:influence:fasn_activity:positive:.evidence: ScienceDirect (Fatty acid synthase and liver TG metabolism, 2011): 'FAS is solely responsible for synthesizing palmitate'; 'FAS participates in liver TG metabolism by contributing de novo synthesized lipids for storage and secretion'. PMC2897101 (FASN in NAFLD): FASN overexpression drives steatosis via DNL. Nature Communications doi:10.1038/s41467-023-44364-y (fatty acid synthesis and PUFA use). NCT02948569 (FASN inhibitor trial, DNL reduction). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, de novo lipogenesis chapter. | intervention: do(fasn_activity UP) raises hepatic de novo lipogenesis flux; do(fasn_activity DOWN/LoF) reduces palmitate synthesis and hepatic DNL
causal:influence:fasn_activity:positive:.mechanism: Fatty acid synthase (FASN, PR:000007348) catalyzes the committed, rate-determining step of hepatic de novo lipogenesis (DNL): serial condensation of malonyl-CoA units onto acetyl-CoA to produce palmitate (C16:0). FASN is the only mammalian enzyme capable of synthesizing palmitate de novo; hepatic_lipogenesis is defined as the flux from acetyl-CoA to fatty acids/triglycerides, which is proportional to FASN activity. Raised FASN expression (e.g. in insulin-stimulated or NAFLD states) directly increases DNL flux; FASN inhibitors (e.g. TVB-2640) reduce hepatic DNL in clinical trials. The causal edge is the direct enzyme-product relationship: do(fasn_activity UP) -> hepatic_lipogenesis UP.

causal:influence:fibrin_clot:positive:pl.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep (fibrin-stimulated tPA/plasminogen activation); Wajima 2009 (plasmin/fibrinolysis sub-network), BioModels BIOMD0000000340

causal:influence:galactocerebrosidase_ac.mechanism: GALC (galactocerebrosidase / galactosylceramidase) cleaves galactosylceramide to ceramide + galactose; galactosylceramide is the primary substrate and accumulates when GALC is deficient (Krabbe disease / globoid cell leukodystrophy)

causal:influence:gcdh_activity:negative:.mechanism: GCDH (glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase) converts glutaryl-CoA to crotonyl-CoA in lysine/tryptophan catabolism; LoF causes glutaryl-CoA accumulation, esterification to glutarylcarnitine (C5-DC), and elevated plasma glutarylcarnitine — the specific NBS marker of glutaric acidemia type I

causal:influence:gcdh_activity:negative:.mechanism: Excess glutaryl-CoA from GCDH deficiency is conjugated with glycine to form glutarylglycine, which is excreted in urine — reduced GCDH raises urinary glutarylglycine

causal:influence:gcdh_activity:positive:.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — glutaric aciduria type 1 (GCDH, OMIM 231670): mitochondrial dysfunction and energy deficit documented; GCDH electrons feed ETC via ETF/ETF-QO. Lehninger Ch.18: FAD-linked acyl-CoA dehydrogenases (including GCDH) donate electrons to ETF for ETC entry. Boy et al. (2017) J Inherit Metab Dis: mitochondrial ATP production impaired in GCDH deficiency. | intervention: Glutaric aciduria type 1 (GCDH LoF, OMIM 231670): ETF electron flux from lysine catabolism impaired; glutaryl-CoA/glutarate mitochondrial toxicity → cellular ATP level reduced
causal:influence:gcdh_activity:positive:.mechanism: GCDH (glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase) catalyses the FAD-linked oxidative decarboxylation of glutaryl-CoA to crotonyl-CoA in lysine/hydroxylysine/tryptophan catabolism; its electrons are transferred via ETF (electron-transfer flavoprotein) to ETF-QO and then to ubiquinone in the mitochondrial ETC, contributing to cellular ATP synthesis. GCDH deficiency (glutaric aciduria type 1) impairs this electron-flux pathway; accumulated glutaryl-CoA and glutaric acid also exert mitochondrial toxicity reducing ETC efficiency. do(GCDH_activity UP) → more ETF-mediated electron flux → ETC → more ATP.

causal:influence:gfr:negative:plasma_cys.mechanism: cystatin C is produced at a constant rate by all nucleated cells, freely filtered, and catabolized by the proximal tubule; plasma cystatin C is inversely related to GFR (an endogenous GFR marker)

causal:influence:ghrelin:positive:pituit.evidence: Farhy 2007 BioModels MODEL0912096133 (PMID 17185408); Williams Endocrinology (ghrelin/GHS-R) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:ghrelin:positive:pituit.mechanism: Ghrelin acts on somatotroph GHS-R1a to amplify GH secretory output, synergistic with GHRH.

causal:influence:gi_parasympathetic_tone.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-080 (15.2: Divisions of the Autonomic Nervous System): parasympathetic system increases digestive secretions; muscarinic receptor activation on secretory cells drives fluid and enzyme secretion throughout the GI tract. causal:influence:gi_parasympathetic_tone.mechanism: Vagal efferents stimulate secretory cells throughout the GI tract: salivary glands (amylase), gastric chief/parietal cells (pepsin/HCl), small intestinal crypts (fluid), and pancreatic acini (enzyme juice) via ACh → M3 receptors. Increased parasympathetic tone globally elevates GI secretion rate.

causal:influence:glcnac_phosphotransfera.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 11 (lysosomal targeting via mannose-6-phosphate); I-cell disease / mucolipidosis II OMIM 252500; Scriver's Online Metabolic Bases 'I-Cell Disease and Pseudo-Hurler Polydystrophy' (Kornfeld & Sly): GNPTAB deficiency causes hypersecretion of all lysosomal hydrolases, with plasma hexosaminidase elevated 10-20x; beta-hexosaminidase is the classic serum diagnostic marker for I-cell disease | intervention: do(GNPTAB activity ↓) = I-cell disease (OMIM 252500): plasma total beta-hexosaminidase elevated 10-20-fold; leukocyte enzyme activity severely reduced
causal:influence:glcnac_phosphotransfera.mechanism: GNPTAB (GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase) adds the mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) targeting signal to lysosomal enzymes including beta-hexosaminidase. Without M6P, enzymes are secreted into the extracellular space instead of reaching lysosomes — I-cell disease / ML II. LoF therefore markedly elevates plasma (serum) beta-hexosaminidase.

causal:influence:glomerular_hydrostatic_.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.26 (Urine Formation by the Kidneys: I. Glomerular Filtration, Renal Blood Flow, and Their Control) §Increased Glomerular Capillary Hydrostatic Pressure Increases GFR: “Increases in glomerular hydrostatic pressure raise GFR, whereas decreases in glomerular hydrostatic pressure reduce GFR.”
causal:influence:glomerular_hydrostatic_.mechanism: higher glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure raises net filtration pressure driving fluid across the filtration barrier, increasing GFR

causal:influence:glucocerebrosidase_acti.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Gaucher Disease section (elevated plasma acid phosphatase as a biomarker of Gaucher disease; reflects macrophage/Gaucher cell activation by lipid-laden lysosomes); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (lysosomal storage diseases: enzyme deficiency → substrate accumulation → macrophage activation). | intervention: loss-of-function of glucocerebrosidase (GBA, Gaucher disease)
causal:influence:glucocerebrosidase_acti.mechanism: Gaucher disease (glucocerebrosidase/GBA deficiency) causes glucosylceramide accumulation in macrophages → Gaucher cell activation → macrophage secretion of tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRACP5b) into plasma. Low glucocerebrosidase activity leads to high plasma acid phosphatase, a well-known clinical marker of Gaucher disease activity.

causal:influence:glycerate_kinase_activi.evidence: D-glyceric aciduria (GLYCTK; OMIM 220120): D-glycerate accumulates in urine, plasma, and CSF (Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases — D-glyceric aciduria: neurological phenotype with D-glycerate in CSF); Scriver's OMMBID | intervention: do(GLYCTK / D-glycerate kinase loss-of-function)
causal:influence:glycerate_kinase_activi.mechanism: D-glycerate kinase (GLYCTK) phosphorylates D-glycerate to 2-phosphoglycerate; GLYCTK deficiency (D-glyceric aciduria) allows D-glycerate to accumulate systemically including in CSF — reduced GLYCTK raises CSF D-glycerate

causal:influence:glyoxylate_reductase_ac.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — primary hyperoxaluria type 2 (GRHPR, OMIM 260000)
causal:influence:glyoxylate_reductase_ac.mechanism: GRHPR reduces glyoxylate to glycolate (detoxification); loss diverts glyoxylate to oxalate, raising urinary oxalate (hyperoxaluria type 2)

causal:influence:haao_activity:negative:.evidence: Kynurenine pathway biochemistry; bioRxiv 2021.06.01.446651 — 'elevating physiological levels of 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid via inhibition of HAAO extends lifespan'; Nature Communications 2023 — HAAO inhibition raises 3-HAA; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (kynurenine pathway: KYNU → 3-hydroxyanthranilate → HAAO → ACMS); note: isolated HAAO deficiency as a clean human IEM is not fully characterised, but HAAO is the definitive enzymatic consumer of 3-HAA in the pathway. | intervention: do(HAAO activity ↓) = HAAO inhibition / kynurenine pathway block at HAAO step
causal:influence:haao_activity:negative:.mechanism: 3-Hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) converts 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (3-HAA) to 2-amino-3-carboxymuconate semialdehyde (the upstream precursor of quinolinate and NAD+) in the kynurenine pathway. Reduced HAAO activity → 3-HAA not consumed → plasma 3-hydroxyanthranilate accumulates (∂[3-HAA]/∂(HAAO activity) < 0). HAAO inhibition experimentally elevates systemic 3-HAA levels in worms and mice.

causal:influence:hal_activity:negative:u.evidence: Histidinemia OMIM 235800; Wikipedia Histidinemia (citing primary literature): 'Formation of Nτ-ribosylhistidine, a novel histidine derivative found in the urine in histidinemia'; Orphanet 2157 histidinemia; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (histidine catabolism, histidinemia as benign inborn error); Lehninger (histidine catabolism, HAL first step). | intervention: do(HAL loss-of-function) — histidinemia OMIM 235800
causal:influence:hal_activity:negative:u.mechanism: HAL (histidine ammonia-lyase/histidase) catalyzes the first step of histidine catabolism (histidine -> urocanate + NH3). HAL deficiency (histidinemia) causes histidine to accumulate; the accumulated histidine undergoes modified catabolism including formation of N-tau-ribosylhistidine (Nτ-ribosylhistidine), a novel histidine derivative found specifically in the urine of histidinemia patients. do(HAL LoF) -> urinary N-tau-ribosylhistidine rises.

causal:influence:hemoglobin_o2_affinity:.evidence: A rightward shift means more unloading of O2 at a given P O2 in a tissue capillary ... By contrast, stored blood in a blood bank may be depleted of 2,3-DPG, which impairs unloading of O2
causal:influence:hemoglobin_o2_affinity:.mechanism: lower O2 affinity (right-shifted curve) increases O2 unloading at a given tissue capillary PO2; higher affinity impairs unloading

causal:influence:hepatic_glucose_product.evidence: Bergman minimal model glucose mass balance (EGP appearance term)
causal:influence:hepatic_glucose_product.mechanism: hepatic glucose output adds glucose to plasma pool

causal:influence:hmg_coa_lyase_activity:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, ketogenesis (HMG-CoA lyase produces acetoacetate from HMG-CoA). causal:influence:hmg_coa_lyase_activity:.mechanism: HMG-CoA lyase cleaves HMG-CoA to acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA, the final step of hepatic ketogenesis; deficiency (HMGCL deficiency, OMIM 246450) abolishes ketone body synthesis, causing hypoketotic hypoglycemia — plasma acetoacetate falls (reduced synthesis). Conversely, elevated HMG-CoA lyase activity drives more acetoacetate production.

causal:influence:leptin:positive:metabol.mechanism: leptin signalling supports sympathetic thermogenic tone and resting energy expenditure; falling leptin during weight loss lowers metabolic rate (adaptive thermogenesis)

causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.mechanism: arterial pressure during ejection sets the load the ventricle ejects against; by Laplace systolic wall stress rises with chamber pressure (quality: arterial pressure -> disposition: ventricular wall mechanics -> quality: afterload)

causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.mechanism: Elevated arterial blood pressure raises capillary hydrostatic pressure, increasing the net outward Starling force and driving more fluid across the capillary wall into interstitial space

causal:influence:metabolic_rate:negative.mechanism: at constant O2 delivery, higher tissue O2 utilization raises extraction and lowers mixed venous PO2/content; conversely impaired mitochondrial utilization raises mixed venous PO2

causal:influence:methionine_synthase_act.evidence: Methionine synthase deficiency cblG (OMIM:250940) — MTR LoF causes hyperhomocysteinemia
causal:influence:methionine_synthase_act.mechanism: RHEA:11172 (EC 2.1.1.13): L-homocysteine is the SUBSTRATE remethylated to methionine, so LoF causes homocysteine to accumulate

causal:influence:mevalonate_kinase_activ.evidence: Mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD/HIDS) OMIM 610377 (MVK LoF); Houten et al., 1999 Hum Mol Genet (isoprenoid pathway block in MVK deficiency); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Ch. 26 (isoprenoid/cholesterol biosynthesis: mevalonate -> phosphomevalonate -> ... -> farnesyl-PP -> farnesol/squalene). | intervention: MVK loss-of-function (mevalonate kinase deficiency): MVK LoF -> reduced farnesyl-PP flux -> reduced plasma farnesol
causal:influence:mevalonate_kinase_activ.mechanism: Mevalonate kinase (MVK) phosphorylates mevalonate, committing flux through the isoprenoid/sterol pathway toward farnesyl-pyrophosphate (farnesyl-PP); farnesol is generated by hydrolysis of farnesyl-PP. Greater MVK activity increases farnesyl-PP production and thus farnesol levels; MVK deficiency (MKD/HIDS) reduces flux through this node.

causal:influence:mitochondrial_complex_i.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-7.1 (7.1: Energy in Living Systems): 'Most of the ATP generated during glucose catabolism... is derived from... chemiosmosis, which takes place in mitochondria'; NAD+ accepts electrons from organic molecules and passes them into the respiratory chain; in type 2 diabetes 'the oxidation efficiency of NADH is reduced, impacting oxidative phosphorylation'.
causal:influence:mitochondrial_complex_i.mechanism: Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) oxidizes NADH and feeds electrons into the mitochondrial electron-transport chain; greater complex I activity drives greater overall respiratory chain electron flux.

causal:influence:mlycd_activity:negative.evidence: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency, OMIM:248360 — LoF causes elevated plasma malonylcarnitine (C3-DC), the cardinal NBS biomarker
causal:influence:mlycd_activity:negative.mechanism: RHEA:18781 (EC 4.1.1.9): malonyl-CoA + H(+) = acetyl-CoA + CO2; malonyl-CoA is the substrate; plasma malonylcarnitine (C3-DC) is the measurable acylcarnitine surrogate of malonyl-CoA accumulation

causal:influence:muscle_coenzyme_q10:pos.evidence: COQ2 mutations cause primary CoQ10 deficiency; CoQ10-deficient patients show decreased quinone-dependent Complex II+III and G3P+III activities (PMC:PMC4705639; Acosta et al., Biol Res 2016). CoQ10 deficiency → decreased electron transport → reduced mitochondrial respiratory chain activity (PMC:PMC4112527). Oral CoQ10 supplementation restores Complex III activity in COQ2 patients. | intervention: do(COQ2 loss-of-function): impaired 4-hydroxybenzoate polyprenylation → reduced CoQ10 biosynthesis → decreased muscle CoQ10 → reduced Complex III substrate availability → decreased Complex III activity
causal:influence:muscle_coenzyme_q10:pos.mechanism: Coenzyme Q10 (ubiquinone) is the obligate electron shuttle between Complex I/II and Complex III in the mitochondrial respiratory chain; COQ2 deficiency → reduced CoQ10 biosynthesis → reduced muscle CoQ10 → insufficient substrate for Complex III ubiquinol:cytochrome c oxidoreductase reaction → decreased Complex III activity and impaired oxidative phosphorylation

causal:influence:nags_activity:positive:.evidence: NAGS deficiency overview (Medscape 941090) — biochemical blockade identical to CPS1 deficiency; low citrulline and high glutamine/ammonia; NAGS deficiency Nature Sci Rep 2021; OMIM 237310 NAGS deficiency. | intervention: NAGS LoF (NAGS deficiency, OMIM 237310): NAGS activity DOWN → no N-acetylglutamate → CPS1 inactive → urea cycle blocked → plasma citrulline DOWN
causal:influence:nags_activity:positive:.mechanism: N-acetylglutamate synthase (NAGS) produces N-acetylglutamate (NAG), the essential allosteric activator of CPS1.
